enunciado: Which goal is achieved by the implementation of private IPv4 addressing on a network?
alternativas: allows servers and workstations to communicate across public network boundaries
provides a reduction in size of the forwarding table on network routers
allows communication across the Internet to other private networks
provides an added level of protection against Internet exposure
explicacao_profunda: Private IPv4 (RFC 1918) is not advertised as public Internet space, so internal hosts are not directly reachable from the global Internet without NAT or a similar edge translation—this reduces direct exposure. The correct answer (“provides an added level of protection against Internet exposure”) captures that protection/conservation role. Option A (“allows servers and workstations to communicate across public network boundaries”) fails because private addresses do not by themselves enable free communication across public boundaries. Option B (“provides a reduction in size of the forwarding table on network routers”) is also incorrect: private addressing does not shrink the global Internet routing table for other enterprises, nor make private-to-private Internet paths routable without tunnels/NAT.

_meta.before_preview: RFC1918 private IPv4 is reused internally without global uniqueness, conserving public space and reducing direct Interne
